## Decision

- Needs reviewer attention before upstream: findings remain.

## Confirmed findings

- Traceability entry lists 3 new tests but the spec body only cites 'connected reverse edge ... at most twice' and 'union of single-root walks, each excluding only its own seed'; the shared-tail test name and the 'at most twice' wording align. No drift found between spec and test mapping.
- crates/ripr/src/analysis/workspace/path_dependencies.rs:763 — In expansion_matches_per_seed_walks_on_all_three_node_graphs the unknown 'ghost/' seed is appended to `changed` for every seed_mask including 0. With seed_mask=0 there are no real seeds but ghost is still treated as a seed; expected therefore contains only ghost's direct callers (or nothing). The asserted equality is still meaningful but the test's variable name 'changed' is misleading when seeds == []. Minor; consider skipping seed_mask==0 or documenting intent.

## Verification questions

- Confirm reverse_reachable_union pushes (neighbor, origin) but does not recheck origin divergence when a parent already has two origins, so a second-origin edge can still be visited even when the origin it carries is already represented. This is bounded but not pruned.

## Refuted

- Thread-local Cell<usize> counter escapes cfg(test) into production binary via cfg(test) attribute leakage or build profile, exposing undefined behavior in shipped artifacts.; refuted because: All three increment sites are wrapped in `#[cfg(test)]`; cargo test compiles with --cfg test, production builds do not. Even if leaked, Cell operations are well-defined for the same thread; no unsafe is used.
- Diff touches Rust only; no JS-backed worker, async runtime, transferable buffer, MessageChannel, or DetachArrayBuffer/ArrayBuffer::detach/transfer is added or crossed. Lane is genuinely out of scope.
- A JS-backed worker or async detach/transfer boundary might leak between Rust expansion callers through seam_cache, ffi, or wasm glue, causing memory safety or aliasing UB.; refuted because: No js/wasm/worker/ffi surface exists in crates/ripr/src/analysis/workspace or its seams; new code uses only std collections and a std::thread_local under cfg(test); no #[unsafe], no Send/Sync expansion, no Box::from(slice)/detachable allocation pattern. Lane is inapplicable.

REVIEW_INCOMPLETE — current advisory findings disposition for exact head 99ff69b63e38a3e0627d859be898e74299f8bb69.

Inspected github-actions review PRR_kwDOSiSx0c8AAAABTJRkCA against current source, including both verification points:

1. Spec/traceability: the provider explicitly found no drift; no repair is requested or needed.

2. Unknown-seed/zero-mask finding: incorrect as a defect; retain this control. The existing test doc already says "Always add an unknown seed, and account independently for the one-hop index." Its graph generator uses only a/b/c endpoints, so ghost has neither a graph node nor any declared-target caller. For seed_mask=0 the expected result is empty, directly checking that an unknown changed package creates no phantom expansion. The variable changed represents changed package roots, including an unknown root; it does not claim the graph has a connected seed. Skipping this case would remove useful negative coverage. See expansion_matches_per_seed_walks_on_all_three_node_graphs in https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/99ff69b63e38a3e0627d859be898e74299f8bb69/crates/ripr/src/analysis/workspace/path_dependencies.rs .

3. Origin-pruning question: confirmed bounded behavior, not a missed bound. reverse_reachable_union rechecks sources at dequeue. An already-seen first origin or any arrival after a second distinct origin continues before reached insertion or neighbor iteration. Each node therefore expands its neighbors at most twice. Duplicate queued arrivals can still occur, but every non-initial enqueue is generated by one of those at-most-two expansions, so they add at most 2E queue entries plus the initial roots; they cannot restore per-root repeated edge work. The accepted second distinct origin is necessary for including a seed reached from another seed, including after paths meet before cycling back. The retained old-DFS oracle, literal cycle/root controls and production-path operation counter already exercise this contract.

No source edit or unchanged expensive proof replay is warranted by these findings. All returned inline threads remain empty. Local proof and the passing exact-head read-only wheel check remain valid. The advisory action step completed successfully, but its receipt-reporter/job closeout is not yet terminal.

Final merge disposition remains REVIEW_INCOMPLETE: required hosted Rust qualification is unestablished and the native Ready handoff was denied by automatic approval review. PR remains Draft; no merge-ready label, alternate CI request, merge, release or deployment was attempted.
